title: release step 11 asks ci.query about the commit alone, so a branch push's green on the release commit ends the release before the tag's run exists -- Gtools v0.4.0 never waited on its macOS leg
body:
FOUND 2026-09-25 by gtools-vc, on Gtools' first real cut with devbin's release core (v0.4.0), and reported to devbin-vc. Confirmed by vc against lib/release.steps at c9e3399.

WHAT HAPPENS. Step 11 asks the project's `release.ci.query` about the release commit alone: release_ci_verdict runs `<query-word>... <sha>` (lib/release.steps, release_ci_verdict; lib/cmd/release step 11), and its contract says the query is run with the sha as its last argument. A release pushes the release commit to its branch and pushes the tag, and CI runs a workflow for each, both on that one sha. At step 11 on Gtools' cut, only the branch push's run existed (36155136723, headBranch main, whose workflow skips the macOS job). The query read every run on the sha, found that one green, and the release ended green without ever waiting on the tag's run (36156500018, which carries the macOS leg). The tag's run passed later, so nothing shipped broken this time; the verdict step still reported a verdict it never measured.

WHO IT REACHES. Every estate that declares `release.ci.query` and runs CI on both a branch push and a tag push of one commit: Gtools, and Utilz, whose tools/ci-state Gtools copied and which reads every run on the sha the same way. devbin's own cut declares no ci.query (step 11 is skipped, and object: ci waits on the release object the tag's workflow makes), so devbin's own releases are not affected.

GTOOLS' LOCAL FIX (gtools f72329b, tools/ci-state): when `git tag --points-at <sha>` names a release tag, only runs whose headBranch is that tag count, and the answer is `none`, kept waiting, until one has registered.

THE FIX FOR devbin, filed into 0.1.8 on hv's ruling of 2026-09-25: step 11 hands the query the release tag as well as the sha, and the contract says a query answers for the tag's runs only, `none` until one exists. The contract change, the pages (release.md, docs/releasing.md, the reference config), and what an existing query that reads only the sha does when handed a second argument are the build's to state; the estates' own queries (Utilz tools/ci-state, Gtools tools/ci-state) are each estate's to update, and the release notes say so. The arms hold a sha with a green branch run and no tag run reading `none`, and a green tag run reading green.

## Resolution

Fixed at 7fa179d. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. Release step 11 runs the project's ci.query as before, `<query-word>... <sha>`, with the release tag in its environment as DEVBIN_RELEASE_TAG, and a query that reads it answers for that tag's runs only, `none` until one exists, which step 11 already waits on. The tag travels in the environment, not as an argument (vc's ruling), since Gtools' and Utilz's tools/ci-state refuse any argument but the sha, and a second one would have failed every cut of theirs after the tag, the push and the object. The cut unsets any DEVBIN_RELEASE_TAG it inherits, so no gate or after: command sees one. Row 11 says what the query answered ("ci.query answers green for v1.0.1 (<sha>): run N"), and "no verdict from ci.query" when it gave none.
- NOT CHANGED, ON THE RECORD. A query that does not read DEVBIN_RELEASE_TAG keeps its old verdict, every run on the sha, and the core cannot tell it from one that reads it: an arm documents that limit, and the 0.1.8 release notes ask Gtools and Utilz to read the tag in their tools/ci-state (Gtools: in place of `git tag --points-at`). ST0007 is closed, so its record is not rewritten and the supersession is recorded here: ST0007 is superseded in part by issue 0149 (devbin 0.1.8) -- step 11's query still runs as `<query-words> <sha>`, and is now also handed the release tag in its environment as `DEVBIN_RELEASE_TAG`, whose runs alone are the verdict for a query that reads it.
- REVIEWS. critic-shell's first pass: 1 critical (the fleet's queries refuse a second argument), 1 warning (a false green), built; its second pass converged, its recommendations taken as v2b. vc's review: vc, 2026-09-25, approved at v2b on the rulings built as ruled, the drives and the evidence below; the final suite over the landed stack is below.
- RED FIRST AND MUTANTS. Each arm red at its own assertion on HEAD's code; the arity arm red on v1's, the critical reproduced. 11 mutants, all killed.
- THE SUITE. All of tests/unit over the six remaining 0.1.8 changes stacked in landing order on a252178 (0134, 0135, 0145, 0149, 0148, 0150), on a clean checkout built from the six exports (head 55f4c7e, tree 840726e0, the build stack's own tree), 2026-09-26 02:11:38Z to 02:46:47Z: 2040 of 2040 ok, 0 not ok, its 5 skips the declared ones (two no-tty branches, two require_command arms that skip off CI, the case-sensitive rename arm on this case-folding disk); the arms that need real cargo ran. Main after the landing is byte-identical to that tree.
